newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended little changed on Thursday, with all eyes turned to the August consumer price data and repo tender on Friday, dealers said.
On average, economists polled by Reuters expect inflation of 3.9 percent in August, up from 3.7 in July.

Nine of 10 surveyed said they believed the central bank would leave its key money market rate steady at 7.25 percent, waiting for details on the government's 1997 budget draft before sanctioning an interest rate reduction.
On Thursday, the market found some support from U.S. data showing price pressures remained moderate.
Core U.S. producer price inflation fell 0.1 percent in August, reinforcing views that U.S. price pressures are not as severe as feared in the summer.
"The outlook on the U.S. economy has changed substantially, helping Treasury bonds higher," a dealer said.
